# Page Object Output Template

The `scaffold-page-object` skill renders generated files following this template. The top-of-file comment block is **mandatory** and identical across every generated file (only the date varies).

## Template

```typescript
// Generated by /scaffold-page-object on YYYY-MM-DD.
// Tests using this Page Object are generated by /from-issue from Jira
// tickets. Manual edits are welcome — this file is not regenerated
// automatically.

import { Header } from '@components/Header'; // one import per detected component
import { step } from '@utils/step';

const PKG = 'com.saucelabs.mydemoapp.android:id';

class <Name>Page {
  // Composed components first (composition rule #6)
  readonly header = new Header();

  // Page-direct locators second, as getters: each access re-queries the screen
  // instead of holding an element that goes stale after a transition.
  get title() {
    return $(`id=${PKG}/productTV`);
  }

  get continueButton() {
    return $('~Confirms products for checkout');
  }

  // A locator for one of many similar elements takes a discriminator and is
  // named for what it discriminates (composition rule #9).
  rowFor(productName: string) {
    return $(
      `android=new UiSelector().text("${productName}")` +
        `.fromParent(new UiSelector().resourceId("${PKG}/removeBt"))`,
    );
  }

  // Action methods — every one a test calls directly wraps its body in ONE step.
  async open(): Promise<void> {
    await step('Open the <name> screen', async () => {
      await this.header.openCart();
      await this.title.waitForDisplayed();
    });
  }

  async remove(productName: string): Promise<void> {
    await step(`Remove "${productName}" from the cart`, () => this.rowFor(productName).click());
  }

  // Queries return data, never an element (composition rule #8), and are NOT steps.
  async getProductNames(): Promise<string[]> {
    return $$(`id=${PKG}/titleTV`).map((e) => e.getText());
  }
}

// No fixtures in WebdriverIO: Page Objects are singletons.
export default new <Name>Page();
```

## Rules

- **Comment block at top** — mandatory; copy verbatim with `YYYY-MM-DD` replaced by today's date.
- **Selector preference order:**
  1. `~accessibility id` (`content-desc`)
  2. `id=<package>:id/<resource-id>`
  3. `-android uiautomator` (`UiSelector`) / `-ios predicate string`
  4. `-ios class chain`
  5. Never XPath — this one fails the build; the rest are judgment.
- **Uniqueness outranks level, and WebdriverIO will not tell you.** `$()` returns the **first** match silently, so an ambiguous locator taps or reads the wrong element and the test may still pass. Count every locator on the screen it belongs to **and** on the screens a test arrives from. The snapshot tool marks ambiguity for you by suggesting `.instance(N)` — that suffix is the count, not the answer.
- **Never ship `.instance(N)` or `$$(sel)[0]`.** Both say "whichever one is third today". Discriminate by text, or by hierarchy (`fromParent`, `childSelector`), at the highest level that yields one match. Say which level you took and why in a comment beside it.
- **Scoping to a container is not a downgrade.** It answers "which screen am I on", not "which element do I act on". Its children stay at their own level.
- **Locators are getters, not fields set in a constructor.** A mobile screen is rebuilt on every transition, and a stored element goes stale (`staleElementReference`). Composed components are `readonly` fields, because a component holds getters of its own.
- **A method never returns another Page.** Return `Promise<void>` or data. Fluent navigation was considered and rejected: it makes every Page know the graph of every Page it can reach, so a routing change edits unrelated files.
- **Never import another Page into a Page.** Same rule from the file system. Two Pages needing the same element means a Component.
- **A Component knows locators and optionally child Components — never a Page, never its parent.** Nesting stops at depth 2 (composition rule #11).
- **Field order** — composed components first, then page-direct locators (composition rule #6).
- **Action method naming** — start from the element's accessible name, normalize to camelCase, strip filler words (`to`, `the`, `and`, `a`, `of`), favour brevity: `"Tap to add product to cart"` → `addToCart`.
- **`step` wraps every action method a test calls, primitives included.** This differs from the Playwright original on purpose: there, a single-element primitive was left unwrapped because the trace auto-records every click. Appium has no trace, so an unwrapped action is invisible in every report and in `/report-bug`'s repro steps. Depth is 1 by construction — a step called inside another step folds into the outer one — so a composed method may call stepped component methods freely.
  - **Queries are not steps.** They read; they are not actions a person would list in repro steps.
  - **Step titles are action-focused, present tense, written for a human reading a failure.** Never put a password or a token in one: titles are written to disk and copied into bug reports.
- **No companion test** — that is `/from-issue`'s job (test generation needs ticket context).
- **No fixture registration.** There is no fixture layer: the spec imports the singleton (`import CartPage from '@pages/CartPage'`). Nothing else needs editing for the Page Object to be usable.
